title: Wren and the Hymn
premise: Rafael Blackwood takes a teaching post at Hollowmere Academy, where students vanish one by one and the staff pretend not to notice. The disappearances trace back to a hymn the school's founders wrote — a song that feeds on children to sustain the founders' descendants, including Rafael's own grandmother, whose house now shows an impossible extra chair in every photograph. Rafael learns she is the last heir of the founding line: the ritual requires her voice to keep the hymn alive, and her refusal means the debt is collected from her students instead. In the end Rafael sings the hymn backward in the founders' sealed chapel, unmaking the bargain at the cost of her own memory of everyone she saved, and walks out of Hollowmere a stranger to the children who owe her their lives.
about_author: Felix Dunmore is the pen name of a former boarding-school music teacher who spent six years collecting local disappearance legends before writing fiction. Wren and the Hymn is his third novel and the first written entirely at night.

chapters.title: The Position
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Rafael. She arrives at Hollowmere Academy for the autumn term, unsettled by the empty desks in her classroom and the headmaster's breezy mention of 'attrition.' The beat is quiet dread beneath professional optimism.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A boy named Colm stops attending; his file simply ends mid-semester. When she asks, colleagues change the subject with practiced smiles. Beat: first crack in the facade.

chapters.title: Grandmother's House
chapters.summary: Weekend visit to Grandma Odile's farmhouse. Rafael notices every family photograph now contains an extra wooden chair no one remembers. Odile goes pale and burns three photos before Rafael can look closer. Beat: inheritance as contamination.

chapters.title: The Hymnal
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Cleaning the school's chapel storage, she finds a hand-bound hymnal with a composition titled 'The Founders' Gratitude,' scored for children's voices. The final page is torn out. Beat: curiosity hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: Colm's Locker
chapters.summary: Rafael opens the abandoned locker and finds sheet music in a child's handwriting, the same hymn, with notes corrected in an adult hand. That night she hears faint singing through the heating vents. Beat: the school is listening back.

chapters.title: Odile's Warning
chapters.summary: Phone call with Odile, who begs Rafael to quit and never sing along if anyone asks. She says only: 'We paid so you wouldn't have to.' Rafael hangs up furious. Beat: family loyalty curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Second Chair
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A second student, Priya, vanishes between periods; teachers mark her absent without comment. Rafael finds Priya's shoes outside the chapel door, neatly paired. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Founders' Portraits
chapters.summary: In the library archive, Rafael studies portraits of the four founders — and recognizes her own jawline in founder Elias Blackwood. The extra chair in grandma's photos matches the one in Elias's portrait. Beat: bloodline horror.

chapters.title: Detention
chapters.summary: Rafael keeps a nervous student, Marcus, late; through the window they both see the chapel lit though it has no electricity. Marcus flees. Rafael alone hears a full choir inside. Beat: denial collapses.

chapters.title: What Odile Signed
chapters.summary: Rafael returns home and confronts Odile, who finally produces a 1974 contract: the Blackwood heirs lend their voices annually so 'the school may continue its harvest.' Odile's payments end this year. Beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She realizes the hymnal's missing final page contains the ritual's completion verse — the part that ends it. Someone removed it deliberately. Beat: hope with a locked door.

chapters.title: Headmaster Vane
chapters.summary: Vane invites Rafael to tea and gently offers her a sabbatical, revealing he knows exactly who she is. 'Your grandmother was punctual about her obligations,' he says. Beat: power wearing courtesy.

chapters.title: Marcus Disappears
chapters.summary: Marcus is gone by morning. Rafael storms the administrative office and finds enrollment records going back a century, each year's losses recorded in ledger columns labeled 'Tithes.' Beat: righteous fury meets institutional calm.

chapters.title: The Choir Loft
chapters.summary: Rafael climbs into the chapel loft at night and finds forty small stools, each engraved with a name and date. The newest stool bears Marcus's name, dated next week. Beat: countdown established.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile admits she sang the hymn every solstice for fifty years, believing she was protecting children from something worse. Her voice is nearly gone; the hymn took it in installments. Beat: sympathy for the complicit.

chapters.title: Interlude: What the Children Hear
chapters.summary: Shifting POV, the vanished students exist in a warm, endless rehearsal room beneath the chapel, singing willingly, forgetting their names note by note. Colm almost remembers his mother. Beat: horror rendered tender.

chapters.title: The Undercroft
chapters.summary: Rafael finds a hidden stair behind the organ and descends into the founders' ritual chamber: a circle of chairs, wax-sealed scores, and a wall of children's shoes. Beat: physical confrontation with the past.

chapters.title: Elias's Journal
chapters.summary: In the undercroft, Rafael reads founder Elias Blackwood's journal: famine year, desperate bargain, the discovery that a Blackwood voice could substitute for many small ones — but only partially, forever. Beat: understanding the mechanism of corruption.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Vane catches Rafael in the undercroft and offers the deal plainly: sing once a year like Odile, and the tithes stop. He shows her Priya alive, singing, serene. Beat: temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Rafael refuses and demands the children be released. Vane sighs, genuinely regretful, and tells her the hymn must be fed by someone — her, or them. He locks the undercroft behind her. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Burning the Hymnal
chapters.summary: Rafael burns her copy of the hymn. That night every photograph in her apartment shows the extra chair moved closer. By dawn it sits beside her bed. Beat: the past refuses erasure.

chapters.title: Allies Among the Guilty
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The aging music teacher, Miss Ferris, secretly approaches Rafael: she copied the final page decades ago out of guilt and has kept it hidden ever since. Beat: unexpected alliance.

chapters.title: The Completion Verse
chapters.summary: Ferris explains the verse must be sung backward, in the founders' chamber, by a Blackwood voice — and that the singer loses what the hymn gave the family: her memories of those she saves. Beat: the true price named.

chapters.title: Odile Objects
chapters.summary: Odile forbids it; she'll sing one more year instead. Rafael sees her grandmother's hands shaking and understands Odile couldn't finish a single verse now. They fight, then embrace. Beat: love against sacrifice.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: The school prepares its winter concert; parents arrive oblivious. Rafael watches rows of children file into the chapel and counts stools in the loft: two new names since Marcus. Beat: dread at maximum pressure.

chapters.title: The Concert
chapters.summary: During the concert, the hymn begins unprompted, rising from beneath the floor. Children's eyes glaze mid-song. Rafael, in the audience, feels her own throat moving without permission. Beat: the inheritance asserting itself.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Rafael wakes in the undercroft circle; Vane and the other descendants have decided not to wait for her consent. The ritual begins above. Beat: betrayal by institution and blood alike.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Room
chapters.summary: POV shifts briefly to Colm: Rafael appears among the vanished children, half-present, her voice being pulled into the hymn. Colm recognizes her and, remembering himself, screams her name. Beat: connection as resistance.

chapters.title: Breaking the Circle
chapters.summary: Ferris and Odile descend into the undercroft and physically shatter the wax seals, disrupting the rite. Vane's composure cracks for the first time. Rafael, half-dissolved into song, reaches for the torn page. Beat: climax ignites.

chapters.title: The Backward Hymn
chapters.summary: Climax. Rafael sings the completion verse reversed while the founders' choir fights her note for note. Chairs topple, photographs burn, the chapel above splits its silence. One by one the children's voices go free. Beat: triumph purchased in advance.

chapters.title: The Cost
chapters.summary: As the last note lands, Rafael's memories of the students begin dissolving — faces, names, the reason she is bleeding and hoarse in a ruined crypt. Odile holds her and weeps. Beat: grief inside victory.

chapters.title: Empty Stools
chapters.summary: Morning. Forty stools stand vacant in the loft. Students reappear across town with no memory of absence, only a strange homesickness. Vane and the descendants are found aged to dust in the chapel pews. Beat: aftermath, uncanny peace.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Kindness
chapters.summary: Colm, restored, encounters Rafael in the corridor and thanks her sincerely for something he can't name. She smiles politely, not knowing him. Beat: bittersweet dramatic irony.

chapters.title: Odile's Photographs
chapters.summary: At the farmhouse, the extra chair is gone from every photo. Odile frames the oldest picture again. Rafael feels she's forgotten something important but cannot grieve what she cannot recall. Beat: quiet mourning.

chapters.title: Resignation
chapters.summary: Rafael tenders her resignation. Vane's office stands empty, already cleared, as if the school anticipated her. The headmaster's chair sits facing the wall. Beat: institutional rot exposed but unresolved.

chapters.title: Miss Ferris's Choice
chapters.summary: Ferris decides to stay and teach honestly, keeping the hymnal's ashes in a jar on her desk as a warning. She and Rafael part as co-conspirators in silence. Beat: responsibility inherited voluntarily.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Rafael hums an unfamiliar melody in the shower and stops, chilled — a fragment of the hymn survived in her body if not her mind. She writes it down and burns the paper. Beat: the past is never fully finished.

chapters.title: Spring Term
chapters.summary: Epilogue-adjacent: a new teacher arrives at Hollowmere, notices the empty desks, and asks Rafael — now leaving — why the attendance rolls have gaps. Rafael says only, 'Ask about the music.' Beat: cyclical unease.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Rafael's POV. On the train away from Hollowmere, a wren lands on her windowsill and sings five perfect notes she somehow knows. She doesn't remember saving anyone, but she cries anyway. Beat: grace without memory — the price of survival, paid in full.
